extracted.intended_audience: aspiring comedians, comedy writers, podcast listeners, and fans of Tim Ferriss interested in the craft of comedy
extracted.subtask_description: Show-notes and interview summary for a podcast episode about Mike Birbiglia's approach to writing, workshopping, performing, and producing comedy (standup, film, books). Includes practical rules, routines, and production notes referenced in the episode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing process and schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Mike's disciplined writing routine, schedule, and use of a 'blessed' journal to generate and refine material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced in show notes and timestamps (e.g., 'Mike talks about his writing routine' [13:14], 'Mike tells us about his “blessed” journal' [17:45]). Implies maintaining a regular schedule, recording ideas, and treating writing as habitual work rather than one-off inspiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use improv and workshops to develop material
rubrics_metrics.description: Harness improv training and iterative workshopping to shape jokes, sketches, and films.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page notes 'the value of improv, and how he workshops his movies' and references UCB Theater and workshopping approaches. Guidance: use improv to test beats, workshop in front of peers or in theater settings to evolve material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Run jokes by trusted peers and solicit specific feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Share material with friends/peers before public performance because 'there are no stakes to showing your friends your work' and to obtain feedback that improves the end result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask targeted questions when soliciting feedback (the episode discusses 'what questions does Mike ask when he wants feedback?' [37:57]). Guidance: run material by a small trusted group, use concrete questions (rather than vague 'how was it?') to get actionable input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious with topical references
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid over-reliance on topical references that can quickly date material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The show notes include 'Why Mike is cautious about being too topical with his references' [22:54]. Implied guidance: favor timelessness or ensure topical jokes have a clear, lasting angle to avoid rapid obsolescence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate choices about profanity and language
rubrics_metrics.description: Be intentional about using curse words on stage; Mike 'generally doesn’t curse on stage.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language choices should fit voice, audience, and material. Avoid gratuitous profanity; consider how word choice affects tone, accessibility, and punch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate storytelling and theatrical elements into standup
rubrics_metrics.description: Blend theater, film, and storytelling techniques with comedy to create a richer solo act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page states Mike's standup 'blends elements of theater, film, storytelling, and comedy.' Guidance: use narrative structure, character, and dramatic pacing to elevate standup beyond isolated jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select stories with genuine stakes and personal truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer material grounded in authentic personal experience and clear stakes (inferred from discussion of story selection and the origin of Sleepwalk With Me).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show notes reference 'the worst advice Mike hears most often (and what he keeps in mind when considering stories to share with an audience)' [1:09:21]. Guidance: choose stories that matter to you and that convey risk, consequence, or emotional truth to engage audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance elements (the 'ratio' for good comedy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain an effective 'ratio' for good comedy (the episode discusses 'What is the “ratio” for good comedy?' [43:37]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page references the concept but does not give a numeric formula. Implied guidance: balance setup vs. payoff, personal vs. observational material, and seriousness vs. punch to optimize comedic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-train in multiple crafts and tie them together
rubrics_metrics.description: Study related crafts (film, theater, writing) deliberately and combine learnings to improve comedic output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page notes Mike 'has been deliberate in studying many crafts and tying them together,' evidenced by success across solo theater, books, film, and radio. Guidance: learn adjacent disciplines to broaden tools and perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop film and long-form projects iteratively
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply iterative workshopping methods when developing films or longer narratives, not just standup bits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notes mention 'how he “workshops” and develops material' and his collaborations (e.g., This American Life). Guidance: test scenes, get feedback, and evolve pacing and structure through staged readings or small screenings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose venues and niches that fit your work
rubrics_metrics.description: Be mindful of venue and career niche; select settings that support the type of comedy you do ('What Mike likes about his career niche (and who he’s really working for)' [1:22:56], 'Mike’s favorite venue in the US' [1:08:37]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match material to venue size, audience expectations, and format. Building a niche/audience can be more effective than trying to please everyone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide accessible transcripts and show notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Make transcripts and detailed show notes available for listeners who prefer reading or need accessibility supports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page links to a transcript of the episode and includes timestamps for topics; comments request easier access to transcripts. Guidance: include full transcripts and searchable timestamps to increase reach and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose sponsors and offers transparently in production
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly present episode sponsors and any promotion details (e.g., Four Sigmatic and Wealthfront with links and discount codes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post includes sponsor messages and links with codes. Guidance: transparently label sponsor content, provide clear links/codes, and integrate sponsor reads in a way that respects audience trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment moderation and civility rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Be cool; critical comments are allowed but rude comments will be deleted. Do not post URLs in comment text; use a personal name or initials rather than a business name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exact wording from the page: 'Remember what Fonzie was like? Cool. Critical is fine, but if you're rude, we'll delete your stuff. Please do not put your URL in the comment text and please use your PERSONAL name or initials and not your business name, as the latter comes off like spam.' This establishes moderation policy and anti-spam guidance for community engagement.
